arxiv-2012-12185.title: A Shell Bonded to an Elastic Foundation and the Existence of Optimal Elastic and Geometric Conditions for the Membrane Case Note: This work is based on a PhD thesis submitted to UCL in 2016 [ 1 ] , and the initial research was funded by The Dunhill Medical Trust [grant number R204/0511] and UCL Impa
arxiv-2012-12185.creator: Kavinda Jayawardana
arxiv-2012-12185.description: Abstract In this article, we derive a mathematical model for a shell (i.e. a thin elastic body) bonded to an elastic foundation by modifying Koiter’s linear shell equations. We prove the existence and the uniqueness of solutions, and we explicitly derive the governing equations and the boundary conditions for the general case.

arxiv-2110-08592.title: Self-stabilizing Byzantine- and Intrusion-tolerant Consensus (preliminary version)
arxiv-2110-08592.creator: Romaric Duvignau, Michel Raynal, Elad M. Schiller
arxiv-2110-08592.description: Abstract One of the most celebrated problems of fault-tolerant distributed computing is the consensus problem. It was shown to abstract a myriad of problems in which processes have to agree on a single value. Consensus applications include fundamental services for the environments of the Cloud or Blockchain. In such challenging environments, malicious behavior is often modeled as adversarial Byzantine faults.

arxiv-2211-08819.title: QCD under extreme conditions
arxiv-2211-08819.creator: Peter Braun-Munzinger, Anar Rustamov, Johanna Stachel
arxiv-2211-08819.description: Abstract In nucleus-nucleus collisions at relativistic energies a new kind of matter is created, the Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP). The phase diagram of such matter and the chemical freeze-out points will be presented in connection to the pseudo-critical temperature for the chiral cross over transition.

arxiv-2302-00612.title: Clinical Decision Transformer: Intended Treatment Recommendation through Goal Prompting
arxiv-2302-00612.creator: Seunghyun Lee, Da Young Lee, Sujeong Im, Nan Hee Kim, Sung-Min Park
arxiv-2302-00612.description: Abstract With recent achievements in tasks requiring context awareness, foundation models have been adopted to treat large-scale data from electronic health record (EHR) systems. However, previous clinical recommender systems based on foundation models have a limited purpose of imitating clinicians’ behavior and do not directly consider a problem of missing values.

arxiv-2303-16661.title: Remote Reactor Ranging via Antineutrino Oscillations
arxiv-2303-16661.creator: S. T. Wilson, C. Cotsford, J. Armitage, N. Holland, M. Malek, J. G. Learned
arxiv-2303-16661.description: Abstract Antineutrinos from nuclear reactors can be used for monitoring in the mid- to far-field as part of a non-proliferation toolkit. Antineutrinos are an unshieldable signal and carry information about the reactor core and the distance they travel. Using gadolinium-doped water Cherenkov detectors for this purpose has been previously proposed alongside rate-only analyses.

arxiv-2308-03484.title: A Systematic Study of Associations between Supernova Remnants and Molecular Clouds
arxiv-2308-03484.creator: Xin Zhou, Yang Su, Ji Yang, Xuepeng Chen, Yan Sun, Zhibo Jiang, Min Wang, Hongchi Wang, Shaobo Zhang, Ye Xu, Qingzeng Yan, Lixia Yuan, Zhiwei Chen, Yiping Ao, Yuehui Ma
arxiv-2308-03484.description: Abstract We universally search for evidence of kinematic and spatial correlation of supernova remnant (SNR) and molecular cloud (MC) associations for nearly all SNRs in the coverage of the MWISP CO survey, i.e. 149 SNRs, 170 SNR candidates, and 18 pure pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe) in 1 ∘ < l < 230 ∘ 1^{\circ}<l<230^{\circ} and − 5 .

arxiv-2401-13249.title: MOS-FAD: IMPROVING FAKE AUDIO DETECTION VIA AUTOMATIC MEAN OPINION SCORE PREDICTION
arxiv-2401-13249.creator: Wangjin Zhou, Zhengdong Yang, Chenhui Chu, Sheng Li, Raj Dabre, Yi Zhao, Tatsuya Kawahara
arxiv-2401-13249.description: Abstract Automatic Mean Opinion Score (MOS) prediction is employed to evaluate the quality of synthetic speech. This study extends the application of predicted MOS to the task of Fake Audio Detection (FAD) as we expect that MOS can be used to assess how close synthesized speech is to the natural human voice.

arxiv-2409-19643.title: 4 ​ b + X 4b+X via electroweak multi-Higgs production as smoking gun signals for Type-I 2HDM at the LHC
arxiv-2409-19643.creator: \firstname Prasenjit \lastname Sanyal \fnsep, \firstname Tanmoy \lastname Mondal \fnsep, \firstname Stefano \lastname Moretti \fnsep, \firstname Shoaib \lastname Munir \fnsep
arxiv-2409-19643.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by \firstname Prasenjit \lastname Sanyal \fnsep, \firstname Tanmoy \lastname Mondal \fnsep, \firstname Stefano \lastname Moretti \fnsep, \firstname Shoaib \lastname Munir \fnsep. Extending the Standard Model (SM) by one additional Higgs doublet leads to the Two-Higgs Doublet Model (2HDM). A specific charge assignment of the SM fermions under the ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} symmetry leads to the Type-I 2HDM. A key feature of the Type-I 2HDM is that all the additional Higgs bosons can be fermiophobic, when their couplings to the SM fermions are suppressed.

arxiv-2502-04867.title: Invariant Image Reparameterisation: Bridging Symbolic and Numerical Methods for Identifiability Analysis, Model Reduction, and Prediction
arxiv-2502-04867.creator: Oliver J. Maclaren, Ruanui Nicholson, Joel A. Trent, Joshua Rottenberry, Matthew J. Simpson
arxiv-2502-04867.description: Abstract Structural and practical parameter non-identifiability issues are common when mathematical models are used to interpret data. Such issues motivate model reparameterisation and reduction methods. Here, we consider Invariant Image Reparameterisation (IIR), which asks when symbolic reparameterisation conditions can be replaced by numerical derivative calculations at a single reference point.

arxiv-2502-16873.title: Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays from Active Galactic Nuclei Jets: The Role of Supermassive Black Hole Growth and Accretion States
arxiv-2502-16873.creator: Olmo Piana *, Hung-Yi Pu *
arxiv-2502-16873.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Olmo Piana *, Hung-Yi Pu *. Jets emanating from active galactic nuclei (AGN) represent some of the most formidable particle accelerators in the universe, thereby emerging as viable candidates responsible for the detection of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs). If AGN jets indeed serve as origins of UHECRs, then the diffuse flux of these cosmic rays would be dependent on the power and duty cycle of these jets, which are inherently connected to the nature of black hole accretion flows.

arxiv-2601-02906.title: Linear Script Representations in Speech Foundation Models Enable Zero-Shot Transliteration
arxiv-2601-02906.creator: Ryan Soh-Eun Shim, Kwanghee Choi, Kalvin Chang, Ming-Hao Hsu, Florian Eichin, Zhizheng Wu, Alane Suhr, Michael A. Hedderich, David Harwath, David R. Mortensen, Barbara Plank
arxiv-2601-02906.description: Abstract Multilingual speech foundation models such as Whisper are trained on web-scale data, where data for each language consists of a myriad of regional varieties. However, different regional varieties often employ different scripts to write the same language, rendering speech recognition output also subject to non-determinism in the output script.

The main goal of postharvest research is to delay senescence and spoilage during shelf life and storage, while preserving and even favoring desirable quality traits.

pmc-11634899.title: Artificial fingerprints engraved through block-copolymers as nanoscale physical unclonable functions for authentication and identification
pmc-11634899.creator: Irdi Murataj, Chiara Magosso, Stefano Carignano, Matteo Fretto, Federico Ferrarese Lupi, Gianluca Milano
pmc-11634899.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Besides causing financial losses and damage to the brand’s reputation, counterfeiting can threaten the health system and global security. In this context, physical unclonable functions (PUFs) have been proposed to overcome limitations of current anti-counterfeiting technologies. Here, we report on artificial fingerprints that can be directly engraved on a wide range of substrates through self-assembled block-copolymer templating as nanoscale PUFs for secure authentication and identification.

pmc-11688791.title: UNDERREPRESENTED FAMILY CAREGIVERS: BUILDING TRUST TO STRENGTHEN RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION
pmc-11688791.creator: Gilbert Gimm, Beth Fields
pmc-11688791.description: The definition of “family caregiver” typically excludes many groups, including those from different genders, racial/ethnic identities, and caregiver age categories. Relationship building, establishing trust with community partners, and interdisciplinary collaborations are essential for the successful recruitment, engagement, and retention of underrepresented family caregivers in research. Moreover, inclusive communication is critical to building trust and strengthening participant engagement.

pmc-11715743.title: Cerebrospinal fluid proteomics identifies biomarkers for discriminating amyloid PET and tau PET stages
pmc-11715743.creator: Zhibo Wang, Yuhan Chen, Jianping Jia
pmc-11715743.description: BackgroundStaging Alzheimer's disease pathology is critical for therapeutic trials and prognosis. Disease staging with amyloid and tau PET provides high accuracy, but this would be more practical with fluid biomarkers. However, current fluid biomarkers are deficient in tracking specific disease stages, especially in advanced stages.

pmc-12558095.title: Exploring Immunological Determinants and Constructing a Predictive Model for Diagnosis of Gout: Insights Into Immune Biomarkers
pmc-12558095.creator: Huanhuan Zeng, Liqiang Zheng, Dan Wu, Xiang Yu, Guangjiang Zhang, Jinwan Du
pmc-12558095.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionImmune-inflammatory mechanisms play a pivotal role in gout pathogenesis, yet the specific immunological signatures and their predictive utility remain underexplored.MethodsThis cross-sectional study enrolled 130 participants (65 gout patients, 65 controls) to compare clinical characteristics, inflammatory markers, and immune profiles. Key variables were selected via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) prediction model was constructed.

pmc-12976213.title: Proteomic profiling of amylases secreted by Penicillium crustosum UEM-45 and characterization of two major enzymes
pmc-12976213.creator: Ketty Carolina Araujo Pacheco, Ione Parra Barbosa-Tessmann
pmc-12976213.description: Despite the industrial relevance of fungal amylases, those from Penicillium crustosum remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to use a proteomics-based approach to identify and characterize extracellular amylases from P. crustosum UEM-45. The extracellular proteome of P. crustosum UEM-45 was analyzed by LC–MS/MS, resulting in the identification of seven amylases among 1,641 extracellular proteins.

pmc-13107465.title: Mechanistic Study of Glycerol Electro-Oxidation on Ni(OH)2/NiOOH Electrodes
pmc-13107465.creator: Youli Yu, Yifeng Wang, Hanzhi Ye, Sid Halder, Guangmeimei Yang, Boxi Ye, Santosh Kumar, Georg Held, James R. Durrant, Maria-Magdalena Titirici, Reshma R. Rao
pmc-13107465.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) is a promising valorization route to upgrade the biodiesel by-product while coproducing green hydrogen at the cathode in electrolyzers. However, the working mechanism of transition-metal-based catalysts such as Ni­(OH)2 remains poorly understood. Here, we employed a multioperando spectroelectrochemical approach combining UV–vis optical spectroscopy, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and time-resolved stepped-potential spectroscopy to investigate the active oxidizing species and charge-transfer dynamics under OER and GOR conditions.

pmc-13233261.title: Gut microbiota and its metabolites with thyroid diseases: functions and mechanisms
pmc-13233261.creator: Chao Jia, Min Li, Xianqiang Yu
pmc-13233261.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The gut microbiota, a complex and dynamic ecosystem of microorganisms residing in the gastrointestinal tract, has emerged as a critical regulator of human physiology, extending its influence far beyond digestion. Recent advances have illuminated the existence of a bidirectional communication network known as the “gut-thyroid axis” which posits that the intestinal microbial community and its vast repertoire of bioactive metabolites are fundamental modulators of thyroid health and disease pathogenesis.

pmc-13473357.title: PT320, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, mitigates nucleus accumbens–associated depression- and anxiety-like behaviors in MitoPark mice of Parkinson's disease
pmc-13473357.creator: Kuan-Yin Tseng, Tung-Tai Kuo, Pi-Kai Chang, Jian-Liang Chou, Eagle Yi-Kung Huang, Nigel H Greig, Ho-Il Choi, Lars Olson, Barry J Hoffer, Yuan-Hao Chen
pmc-13473357.description: BackgroundNeuropsychiatric symptoms such as anxiety and depression substantially impair quality of life in Parkinson's disease (PD), yet the underlying neural circuits remain poorly defined. The MitoPark (MP) mouse, a dopaminergic mitochondrial dysfunction model, recapitulates both motor and non-motor features of PD.

pmc-13506754.title: The embedded documentation of implementation tracking (EDIT): a low-burden approach to supporting implementation documentation in health research
pmc-13506754.creator: Alexis Zollo, Rebecca F. Hamm, Meghan B. Lane-Fall, Laura Ellen Ashcraft
pmc-13506754.description: IntroductionEffectiveness studies often generate rich insights about implementation processes and context. However, formal implementation evaluation is often challenging to incorporate for many reasons, including limited staffing, competing study priorities, lack of implementation expertise, or the absence of dedicated funding. As a result, relevant implementation information is inconsistently documented or lost altogether.
